connections.why: Scarcity and choice are resolved through the demand and supply of markets
Firms make output decisions from costs, revenue and market prices
Profit-maximising behaviour differs across competitive and monopoly structures
Labour is a factor market governed by the same demand and supply forces
Aggregate demand and supply build on individual market behaviour
The AD/AS model explains growth, inflation and employment outcomes
Policy is chosen to move the economy towards its objectives
Fiscal and monetary policy shift aggregate demand and supply
Monetary policy operates through the banking and financial sector
The balance of payments and competitiveness link to the global economy
Global competition shapes the structure and conduct of domestic firms
Employment and wage outcomes are a key macroeconomic objective
Synoptic questions apply market analysis to current micro issues
Synoptic questions evaluate macro policy in real-world contexts
Evaluative judgements rest on quantitative analysis of evidence
Macro evaluation draws on data handling and quantitative skills
Firm behaviour is a frequent focus of synoptic application
